sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Pri. Secy. Home Lko

Counsel for Applicant :- Rajiv Kumar Bajpai, Abdul Shadab Khan, Paresh Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

2. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the informant was married to one Jagdeep Singh Kushwaha, who died in the year 2015 and thereafter the applicant, who was also working in the State Bank of India became close to the victim and used to meet her very often and subsequently physical relations were also formed in between them over a span of almost five years.
It was alleged that the applicant used to take advantage of the situation of the informant allegation with regard to certain money was also made.
The statement under Section 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. also similar statements were made.
The applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 15.10.2023.
Chandan Jain vs State Of U.P. Thru. Pri. Secy.

3. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.

4. Considering the fact that informant is aged about 40 years and physical relations spanned in between the applicant and the victim over a period of 4-5 years, a case for bail is made out as there is no allegation of threat being used for forming of physical relations over a span of five years, the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 15.10.2023 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Chandan Jain be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 0388 of 2023, under Sections 376, 406, 420, 506 IPC, Police Station Gudamba, District Lucknow, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 16.1.2024 Arun  Chandan Jain vs State Of U.P. Thru. Pri. Secy. Home Lko on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105701564/
